Subject: Kraken Health — recap and quick clarifications on prompt output / PII storage

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our demo and the handful of concrete follow-ups you asked for on PII and prompt-output handling so your security and procurement teams can advance the review: 

What we covered (short):
- Default hosted behavior: transient inference cache + request logs retained for operational telemetry.
- Options to reduce or eliminate stored user-visible outputs (ephemeral mode, private deployment).
- Data residency controls per customer and audit logging exports for compliance.

Your asks / follow-ups we promised:
1) A clear statement of what is stored by default for prompts and generated outputs (what, where, how long).
2) Whether embeddings or derived artifacts are persisted and how to opt-out.
3) How audit traces and token-level logs are retained and whether they contain PII.
4) Example artifacts (SOC2 mapping + a compact evidence list) for procurement.

Quick answers (summary) — we will follow up with a short technical note from Marcus and the SOC2 evidence pack attached:
- Prompt inputs: by default, text inputs sent to our hosted API are logged for 30 days and used for billing, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. Logs are stored in the region selected at account creation (US or EU).
- Generated outputs (model responses): not persisted to long-term customer buckets unless a customer enables the persist_outputs flag or saves responses via the Console. Short-lived inference cache (KV cache) is ephemeral (TTL ~ 2 minutes) and is not written to disk as a customer-accessible artifact.
- Embeddings: calculated embeddings are persisted to the customer’s index only if save_embeddings=true; otherwise, a transient vector is created for the call and discarded.
- Audit/tracing: request metadata (timestamps, model id, call latencies, request id) is retained for 90 days for troubleshooting; payloads are included in logs only under default settings but can be redacted or disabled via account controls.
- Private / VPC: in Private deployments we support zero-retention modes and on-prem storage; in that case, nothing leaves the customer network unless explicitly configured.

Next steps we propose:
- Marcus will send a short tech appendix with exact retention windows and config flags (expected by EOD PT).
- We’ll share our SOC2 evidence list and a minimal set of screenshots showing the Console controls (attached).
- If procurement wants, we can provision a 7-day eval account with logging set to minimal retention for an internal pilot.

Attachments: redwood-data-sheet.pdf (product summary), kraken-soc2-questions.xlsx (initial evidence worksheet)

Thanks — I’ll let Marcus add the technical specifics.

—
Aisha Rahman

Hi Samantha — thanks for the precise questions. A couple of technical clarifications to help your engineers and security reviewers: 

1) Access & encryption
- All hosted customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. We use customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted accounts use Redwood-managed KMS by default (we can transition to customer KMS on request).
- Logs that include prompt/response payloads are accessible to limited Redwood SRE/Security personnel under a role-based access policy and only for operational/debug reasons; access is audited and requires justification.

2) Short vs long-term persistence (defaults and config flags)
- prompt_inputs_retention_days: 30 (default, hosted). Can be set to 0 for no storage of prompt payloads; note this disables some quality-monitoring features.
- persist_outputs: false (default). If set to true, generated outputs are written to the customer object store and appear in Console exports.
- inference_kv_cache_ttl_seconds: 120 (ephemeral cache used during streaming/generation; not a customer-visible store).
- embeddings_persistence: off by default; set save_embeddings=true to persist indices.

3) PHI and export actions
- If your integration writes model outputs into your EHR via your backend, that write happens under your control. Redwood will not mirror or persist EHR writes unless persist_outputs is enabled for your account. For the pilot we can preconfigure the account with prompt_inputs_retention_days=0 and persist_outputs=false so no payloads are retained in Redwood logs.

4) Pilot attestation and onboarding
- We can provide a one-page attestation describing the pilot configuration and logging minimization (signed by Redwood security) within 48 hours once procurement confirms the scope.
- For Private customers, we can ship an on-prem package that never transmits payloads to Redwood control plane; that would meet the strictest requirement.

If helpful, I can paste an example curl showing the flags to disable storage. Also attaching a short appendix with the exact config names (see attached redwood-data-sheet.pdf for the table).
